newsitem.title: KENYA: Ruling party, opposition youths clash in Nairobi.
newsitem.headline: Ruling party, opposition youths clash in Nairobi.

text.p: Supporters of the ruling Kenya African National Union (KANU) party clashed with opposition supporters outside parliament in Nairobi on Thursday, witnesses said.
Witnesses said 50 youths shouting slogans in support of KANU and 50 youths allied with opposition parties confronted each other on the road outside the parliament building in the Kenyan capital.
They threw stones and chased each other with sticks.
Police inside parliament fired five times in an attempt to disperse the opposition supporters outside but it was unclear if the shots were live ammunition, rubber bullets or baton rounds.
Two people were injured by flying stones, witnesses said. The clashes were triggered by a row between an opposition-backed alliance pressing for constitutional reforms before elections and KANU.
Opposition party parliamentarians inside the parliament building accused KANU of deliberately bringing the youths to parliament to harass them as they entered or left the building.

KANU said on Wednesday it would not discuss constitutional reforms with the National Convention Executive Council (NCEC), an alliance of opposition-backed groups campaigning for reforms before a general election, because it was a non-elected body.
The NCEC said it had a popular mandate for dialogue and plans a rally in the Indian Ocean city of Mombasa on Saturday.
